component MethodStaticArgCases
export Executable

(* A dotted method call that writes no static argument takes the method's own static arguments from the arguments' types: sizes, types inside other types, a type that is a parameter's whole type, a generic receiver and bounded parameters. *)

object Cell[\T\](v: T) end

object Sized[\nat k\](v: ZZ32)
    idx[\nat j\](b: Sized[\j\]): Sized[\k\] = self
    sz[\nat j\](b: Sized[\j\]): ZZ32 = j
end

object Vec
    first[\T extends { Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }\](v: Vector[\T,3\]): T = v.get(0)
    len[\T extends { Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }, nat n\](v: Vector[\T,n\]): ZZ32 = n
end

object Plain
    id[\T\](x: T): T = x
end

shown(v: Any): String = typecase v of
    v1: ZZ32 => v1.asString || ":ZZ32"
    v2: ZZ64 => v2.asString || ":ZZ64"
    else => "other"
  end

object Mixed
    same[\T\](a: T, b: T): String = "[" || shown(a) || "," || shown(b) || "]"
end

object Holder[\U\](u: U)
    get[\T\](b: Cell[\T\]): T = b.v
    both[\T\](b: Cell[\T\]): (U, T) = (u, b.v)
end

trait Shape end
object Circle extends Shape end
object Within[\R\]()
    pick[\K extends R\](x: K): String = "picked"
end

trait Numbered[\R\]
    num[\N extends Number\](x: N): N = x
end
object Numbers extends Numbered[\String\] end

run(): () = do
    z: ZZ32 = 3
    w: ZZ64 = widen(4)
    assert(Sized[\3\](7).idx(Sized[\2\](5)).v, 7, "a size of the method's own is fixed by an argument of type Sized[2]; inference.tex, section \"The Static Arguments of a Call\"")
    assert(Sized[\3\](7).sz(Sized[\2\](5)), 2, "the size fixed by the argument is the method's j")
    assert(Vec.first(vector[\ZZ32,3\](7)), 7, "a type parameter is fixed by a Vector argument")
    assert(Vec.len(vector[\ZZ32,3\](7)), 3, "a size is fixed by a Vector argument")
    assert(Plain.id(z), 3, "a type parameter that is a parameter's whole type takes the argument's type")
    assert(Mixed.same(z, z), "[3:ZZ32,3:ZZ32]", "two ZZ32 arguments fix T = ZZ32")
    assert(Mixed.same(z, w), "[3:ZZ64,4:ZZ64]", "a ZZ32 and a ZZ64 fix T = ZZ64, the narrowest type into which both convert, and the ZZ32 is converted")
    assert(Holder[\String\]("s").get(Cell[\ZZ32\](z)), 3, "a generic receiver's method takes its own static argument from the argument")
    (p, q) = Holder[\String\]("s").both(Cell[\ZZ32\](z))
    assert(p, "s", "the receiver's static argument stays its own")
    assert(q, 3, "the method's static argument comes from the argument")
    assert(Within[\Shape\]().pick(Circle), "picked", "a bound that names the object's own static parameter admits the argument")
    assert(Numbers.num(z), 5 - 2, "a trait's generic method with a library bound takes its static argument from the argument")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

component NestedReductionFusion
import List.{...}
import Generator2.{...}
export Executable

(* A reduction of reductions over the prefixes of a list answers the same with and without fusion, whether or not the inner reduction distributes over the outer one. *)

sumSum(gg: Generator[\Generator[\ZZ32\]\]): ZZ32 =
    __bigOperator2[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,Generator[\ZZ32\]\](
        SUM[\ZZ32\](), SUM[\ZZ32\](), gg, fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x)

maxMax(gg: Generator[\Generator[\ZZ32\]\]): ZZ32 =
    __bigOperator2[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,Maybe[\ZZ32\],ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,Maybe[\ZZ32\],ZZ32,Generator[\ZZ32\]\](
        BIG MAX[\ZZ32\](), BIG MAX[\ZZ32\](), gg, fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x)

maxSum(gg: Generator[\Generator[\ZZ32\]\]): ZZ32 =
    __bigOperator2[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,Maybe[\ZZ32\],ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,Generator[\ZZ32\]\](
        BIG MAX[\ZZ32\](), SUM[\ZZ32\](), gg, fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x)

minSum(gg: Generator[\Generator[\ZZ32\]\]): ZZ32 =
    __bigOperator2[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,Maybe[\ZZ32\],ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,Generator[\ZZ32\]\](
        BIG MIN[\ZZ32\](), SUM[\ZZ32\](), gg, fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x)

sumProd(gg: Generator[\Generator[\ZZ32\]\]): ZZ32 =
    __bigOperator2[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,Generator[\ZZ32\]\](
        SUM[\ZZ32\](), PROD[\ZZ32\](), gg, fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x)

unfused(f: Generator[\Generator[\ZZ32\]\] -> ZZ32, gg: Generator[\Generator[\ZZ32\]\]): ZZ32 = do
    switchDispatching(false)
    r = f(gg)
    switchDispatching(true)
    r
end

run(): () = do
    l = <|[\ZZ32\] 1, 3, 2 |>
    assert(unfused(sumSum, inits l), 11, "the sum of the prefix sums of 1, 3, 2 without fusion is 11")
    assert(sumSum(inits l), 11, "the sum of the prefix sums of 1, 3, 2 is 11; a sum does not distribute over a sum")
    assert(unfused(maxMax, inits l), 3, "the maximum of the prefix maxima of 1, 3, 2 without fusion is 3")
    assert(maxMax(inits l), 3, "the maximum of the prefix maxima of 1, 3, 2 is 3; a maximum does not distribute over a maximum")
    assert(unfused(maxSum, inits l), 6, "the maximum prefix sum of 1, 3, 2 without fusion is 6")
    assert(maxSum(inits l), 6, "the maximum prefix sum of 1, 3, 2 is 6")
    assert(unfused(minSum, inits l), 1, "the minimum prefix sum of 1, 3, 2 without fusion is 1")
    assert(minSum(inits l), 1, "the minimum prefix sum of 1, 3, 2 is 1")
    assert(unfused(sumProd, inits l), 10, "the sum of the prefix products of 1, 3, 2 without fusion is 10")
    assert(sumProd(inits l), 10, "the sum of the prefix products of 1, 3, 2 is 10")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

component MethodStaticArgInheritedGeneric
export Executable

(* A generic method inherited from a trait, alone under its name, called with no static argument, takes its static argument from the argument's type. *)

trait Tagged[\L\] getter tag(): String end
object NoPair[\L\] extends Tagged[\L\] getter tag(): String = "none" end
object SomePair[\L\] extends Tagged[\L\] getter tag(): String = "some" end
trait Lifted[\T\] end

trait Red[\R,L\]
    distribute[\K\](r: Red[\R,K\]): Tagged[\K\] = NoPair[\K\]
end
object Mx[\T\] extends Red[\T, Lifted[\T\]\] end
object Sm[\T\] extends Red[\T,T\]
    distribute(r: Mx[\T\]): Tagged[\Lifted[\T\]\] = SomePair[\Lifted[\T\]\]
end

kind(x: Any): String = typecase x of
    NoPair[\ZZ32\] => "NoPair[ZZ32]"
    NoPair[\Lifted[\ZZ32\]\] => "NoPair[Lifted[ZZ32]]"
    SomePair[\Lifted[\ZZ32\]\] => "SomePair[Lifted[ZZ32]]"
    else => "other"
  end

run(): () = do
    assert(kind(Mx[\ZZ32\].distribute(Sm[\ZZ32\])), "NoPair[ZZ32]", "the generic method alone under its name takes K = ZZ32 from an argument of type Red[ZZ32,ZZ32]; inference.tex, section \"The Static Arguments of a Call\"")
    assert(kind(Mx[\ZZ32\].distribute(Mx[\ZZ32\])), "NoPair[Lifted[ZZ32]]", "the generic method alone under its name takes K = Lifted[ZZ32] from an argument of type Red[ZZ32,Lifted[ZZ32]]")
    println("PASS")
  end

end
=====
component MethodStaticArgOverloadedReceiver
export Executable

(* A generic method inherited from a trait beside a plain overload of the receiver, called with no static argument, takes its static argument from the argument's type where the plain overload does not apply. *)

trait Tagged[\L\] getter tag(): String end
object NoPair[\L\] extends Tagged[\L\] getter tag(): String = "none" end
object SomePair[\L\] extends Tagged[\L\] getter tag(): String = "some" end
trait Lifted[\T\] end

trait Red[\R,L\]
    distribute[\K\](r: Red[\R,K\]): Tagged[\K\] = NoPair[\K\]
end
object Mx[\T\] extends Red[\T, Lifted[\T\]\] end
object Sm[\T\] extends Red[\T,T\]
    distribute(r: Mx[\T\]): Tagged[\Lifted[\T\]\] = SomePair[\Lifted[\T\]\]
end

kind(x: Any): String = typecase x of
    NoPair[\ZZ32\] => "NoPair[ZZ32]"
    NoPair[\Lifted[\ZZ32\]\] => "NoPair[Lifted[ZZ32]]"
    SomePair[\Lifted[\ZZ32\]\] => "SomePair[Lifted[ZZ32]]"
    else => "other"
  end

run(): () = do
    assert(kind(Sm[\ZZ32\].distribute(Sm[\ZZ32\])), "NoPair[ZZ32]", "beside a plain overload that does not apply, the generic method takes K = ZZ32; overloading.tex, section \"Applicability to Dotted Method Calls\"")
    assert(kind(Sm[\ZZ32\].distribute(Mx[\ZZ32\])), "SomePair[Lifted[ZZ32]]", "the plain overload, more specific than the generic method, runs where it applies")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

content.content:
138:- Resolution: it takes its bound on both paths. Under walk, one whose bound names itself stays open, and a big operator without static arguments takes them from its value or its elements (both below). Walk still gives `Bottom` to these:
153:- Resolution: walk leaves the parameter open. Wherever walk checks a value against the open parameter, every value passes. A generic type that holds the open parameter admits no more than it admits at `Bottom`. A printed type shows the open parameter as `OPEN`: `BoxU[\OPEN\]` for an object `BoxU[\T\]`. A reduction now takes its static arguments by the next entry, and leaves such a parameter open only where it has neither a declared type nor an element.
154:- Reason: an open parameter refuses no value.
158:- Original: the specification desugars a reduction or a comprehension by the type of its expression: for generators `gs`, `SUM[gs] e` of type `N` calls `SUM[\N\]`, and `<| e | gs |>` of type `List[\E\]` calls `BIG <|[\E\]|>` (`Specification/advanced/parallelism-locality/defining-generators.tex`). Walk gave the big operator's static parameters `Bottom`, or left them open where their bound names them. So an empty `SUM` of `RR64` values gave the integer 0, and `Set`'s `BIG UNION` and `BIG INTERSECTION` stopped at their first element. The library left `__bigOperator`'s local function `body(i)` untyped. It declared `IntMap`'s comprehension operator to return an `IntMap[\Val\]`, while its body is a `Comprehension`.
161:  2. else at the join, the least common supertype, of its elements' run-time types; walk collects the elements before it reduces them. Where the join is outside the bound, such as `Number` for `ZZ32` and `RR64` elements of a `SUM`, the parameter stays open, and each `+` runs at its operands' types;
162:  3. else, with no element, at each parameter's bound, or open where the bound names the parameter.
165:  - an empty one that no declared type directs leaves `SUM`'s parameter open, and gives the integer 0, whatever its body's type (ledger row 716);
194:- Resolution: the clause is restored, and the specification allows a where-clause variable in a listed type. In the checker, a value of such a trait, passed where the listed type is expected, binds the call's `nat` parameter to the value's own size. That size is known to equal only itself: two values passed in one call have two sizes, and the size does not reach a type that names another size. Walk loads the clause and binds each size at dispatch, as before, so it runs such a call. The compiled run waits for the switch-over (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXNatOpenRun.fss`).
247:**The trivial open range `(:)`**

\subsection{The inference of a call's static arguments}
\seclabel{revival-inference}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected sections] \chapref{type-inference}; \secref{ranges};
\secref{basic-integers}; \secref{revival-ranges}; \secref{revival-notrevised}.
\item[Change] \chapref{type-inference}, which held a heading and two draft
notes, states how the static arguments of a call that does not write them are
inferred, for type parameters and for \KWD{nat} and \KWD{int} parameters.
The declaration is chosen first, as \secref{resolving-coercion} chooses it, a
declaration with static parameters being applicable to a call if some instance
of it within its bounds is, and compared on the parameter types it declares.

A declared type fixes a type parameter that the return type of a call written

Where the conversions of a numeral tie, the \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} declaration or
instance is taken; where another argument's conversions tie, the call is a

A \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} parameter may be a component of a range, as in the
specification's own examples.
The overloading chapters compare declarations on the parameter types they
declare and infer static arguments after the selection, and \secref{type-param}
gives a type parameter without an \KWD{extends} clause the bound \TYP{Any}
(\secref{revival-overloading}, \secref{revival-bound}).
A type parameter that nothing at a call fixes is instantiated at its bound
under the expected type and never at \TYP{BottomType}: a call whose compiled
run failed loading an instance over \TYP{BottomType}, or failed verification
where the call's result was carried as one, now runs; a call with no expected
type whose type parameter is declared \EXP{\KWD{extends} \TYP{Any}} is
accepted; and a call where the bound and the expected type have no common
subtype, such as a type parameter bounded by \TYP{Object} where \TYP{()} is
expected, is a static error unless the result of the instance at the bound
converts to the expected type.
The compiled type checker departed from the chapter in five cases, each gated
by an expected failure of its tests, until it was revised with the item above:
the expected type could let a declaration applicable only with coercion be

(row~508 of the revival's gap ledger); a call that the rule instantiates at the

content.content:
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A.
The revival decided on 26~September 2026 that a generic call over two different
integer types infers the narrowest type that both coerce into, by a rule
written into this chapter; on 27~September 2026 that the compiled type checker
infers static arguments with coercion and keeps the expected type at a call
written as \EXP{f(x)}, with a retry without it so that a coercion of the result
still applies, and that the chapter is written with it; and on 28~September
2026 that a coercion makes a call possible and never changes which declaration
runs when one is applicable without it, the declaration chosen being then
instantiated by that rule, that a numeral whose conversions tie is read as a
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and that a \KWD{nat} parameter used as a value converts to
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} as a numeral does.
\chapref{multiple-dispatch}, \secref{idn-ref} and \secref{dotted-method-calls}
said that static arguments are inferred as \chapref{type-inference} describes,
and it described nothing; once the compiled type checker infers them by a rule
the text does not state, the text and the implementation disagree, so the
chapter states the rule the checker was built to, and the effect below lists
where the checker departs from it.
The bound in place of the union is the rule by which the dispatcher of the type
group's paper of 2019 instantiates a type parameter that the arguments do not
fix, the intersection of its upper bounds, never \TYP{BottomType}; the team
had assumed the union of the lower bounds, of which the authors write ``we were
unable to complete the proofs of correctness'' (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu,
``Polymorphic Symmetric Multiple Dispatch with Variance'', POPL 2019,
Section~5.4).
The paper gives no algorithm for static inference and asks of it only that it
never instantiate at \TYP{BottomType}; its one example of a static call is
typed at the union of its arguments' types.
The revival decided on 29~September 2026 to take the paper's rule for static
inference as well, which the paper allows and does not require.
The same rule gives a type parameter that neither an argument nor the expected
type fixes the intersection of its upper bounds: the paper's solving step
``never instantiates method type parameters with Bottom'' (Section~5.2), which
answers the question the Working Draft's own note asks, whether type inference
may infer \TYP{BottomType} for a static parameter.
The reasoning for that item, and for the order in which the compiled type
checker tries a call, is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/decision-record.md}
in the revival's repository.
The revival's decision of 29~September 2026 provided that the interpreter
follow the same rule where it instantiates a declaration, from the run-time
types of the arguments; it has no static return type to add to the bound,
except, since 14~October 2026, the declared type of a local variable or of a
top-level or local function whose value is a reduction or a comprehension that
writes no static argument (below).
It departs from the rule for the type parameters that the two boxes name,
three kinds by decision and the others as defects.
Until 9~October 2026, by decision, a type parameter whose bound mentions the
type parameter itself kept \TYP{BottomType}: it has no bound to take before its
own instance is known, the paper's calculus admits no type parameter of a
method in an upper bound (p.~11:11), and the revival had not decided that case.
The revival decided on 8~October 2026 that the interpreter leaves such a type
parameter open where nothing at a call fixes it: it does not instantiate it,
and it admits every value where it checks a value against that type.
An open type parameter is no instance: the rule that inference never
instantiates a static parameter at \TYP{BottomType} keeps a call from an
instance that admits no value, and an open parameter refuses none.
The reasoning is in \nolinkurl{explorations/reviews/p1-judgement.md} in the
revival's repository.
Until 14~October 2026, by decision, a big operator's static parameter whose
bound does not mention it, that a reduction or a comprehension does not write,
kept \TYP{BottomType}: it is the element type of the reduction, which this
chapter does not yet describe, and from \TYP{BottomType} the interpreter's
library builds a comprehension's collection at the type of its elements, where
from the bound it would build it at the bound.
The revival decided on 14~October 2026 that the interpreter instantiates such a
big operator as the desugaring by the type \VAR{N} of the expression would
(\secref{revival-reductions}), with run-time types in place of \VAR{N}: by the
declared type of the local variable, or the declared return type of the
top-level or local function, whose value the reduction or the comprehension is,
which is the static return type that the rule above lets
constrain the instance, and otherwise by the join of the run-time types of the
elements that its generator clauses give, which fix the parameter as \VAR{N}
would and so are not the value's type of a parameter that nothing fixes; where
there is neither, the parameter takes its bound, or is left open where the
bound mentions it.
The reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/perf-probes/walk-plain-bound/REPORT.md} and
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-elements/REPORT.md} in the
revival's repository.
By decision, a type parameter that only the bound of a type parameter that the
arguments fix mentions takes the arguments' type: the interpreter has no
expected type to fix it, and the library's operator that appends two covariant
collections builds its result at such a type parameter, which at its bound
would be \TYP{Any}.
By decision, a lone type parameter whose bound mentions a static parameter,
itself or another, keeps the narrowest named common supertype of the arguments
rather than its bound: the interpreter cannot evaluate such a bound before the
instances are known, and keeping the candidates it had leaves unchanged the
case of a type parameter whose bound mentions itself and that the arguments
fix, which the revival has not yet decided.
As defects, each gated by an expected failure of the revival's tests, the
interpreter erases to \TYP{BottomType} a type parameter declared with several
bounds that it cannot meet, having no intersection type, and a type parameter
that only the result of a function expression without a declared return type
fixes, since it gives that result the type \TYP{BottomType}.
Until 3~October 2026 it also erased a type parameter that an argument bounds
only from above, taking the lower end of the interval that the arguments give
the type parameter; it now takes the upper end, the intersection of the upper
bounds that the rule gives, except, as defects gated by expected failures, for
a type parameter whose bound mentions a static parameter, which it cannot
evaluate before the instances are known, and one declared with several bounds
that it cannot meet.
The reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-instance/decision-record.md}
in the revival's repository.
The order, a declaration chosen and then instantiated, is that of
\secref{resolving-coercion}, read on the parameter types that declarations
declare, as the type group's paper of 2011 reads a declaration with static
parameters: it ``is applicable to a type if and only if at least one of its
instances is'' (\nolinkurl{Papers/Types/setup.tick}, lines 396--397, in the
revival's repository).
The numeral's default is what the interpreter did before this change, giving
a numeral the narrowest of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} and
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} that holds its value, \library\ declaring their numeral type
below \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}; the compiled path, whose library declares its
numeral type beside \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and excluding it, took one of the
declarations that a numeral left tied, and not always the same one (row~391 of
the revival's gap ledger).
It is also the Java programming language's type for an integer literal.
The compiled type checker gives a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} parameter used as a
value the type of a numeral, and the interpreter makes it a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32},
so an \KWD{int} parameter is read as a \KWD{nat} parameter is; on the Java
Virtual Machine the length and the indices of an array are 32-bit integers.
The team's later Types chapter (Luchangco, 2012) gives the coercion relation,
the coercion of a generic type and the valid instantiations of a quantified
type (\nolinkurl{Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick}, lines
938--947, 393--400 and 771--789, in the revival's repository) and never uses
the word ``infer''; the type group's paper leaves the run-time inference of the
static arguments of a dispatched declaration ``beyond the scope of this paper''
(\nolinkurl{Papers/Types/rules.tick}, lines 118--129).
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-inference/decision-record.md}

The team's 2012 patent applications (US~8,843,887 and US~8,898,632;
Chase, Steele, Naden, Hilburn, and Luchangco) relax the rule for a
self-typed parameterized trait: a type may be a subtype of several of its
instantiations when they form a chain.
The revival built that rule whole as an experiment and measured it.
It closes the unsoundness that instantiation exclusion guards against only
together with a rule on return types over every level of a chain and a
change in how a call chooses among generic methods specialised to
different instantiations: 188 lines of code in five files of the compiled
type checker and code generator.
Reversing route~A for route~C would also need a method per level of a
chain in the code generator, work in the interpreter, a way past a stack
overflow of the type checker on the self-typing clauses, and seven library
declarations, besides undoing the reorganization of the library's numeric
types.
Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2976:reads them; a definition at the abstract method's own parameter type is the
Specification/basic/inference.tex:285:dispatches a converted call again, except a call of an overloaded method.}

component MBesideTrait
export Executable
(* a generic dotted method beside a plain one of one name, declared in a trait that an object extends *)
trait Shape comprises { Circle, Square } end
object Circle extends Shape end
object Square extends Shape end
trait Describes
  describe[\T extends Shape\](x: T): String = "generic"
  describe(x: Circle): String = "circle"
end
object Describer extends Describes end
run(): () = do
    println("MBesideTrait start")
    println("MBesideTrait circle: " Describer.describe(Circle))
    println("MBesideTrait square: " Describer.describe(Square))
  end
end
EOF
cat > MBoolTrait.fss <<'EOF'
component MBoolTrait
export Executable
(* a trait's method whose parameter type has a bool static argument, in a trait that an object extends *)
object Flag[\bool b\](v: ZZ32) end
trait Unflags
  unflagTrue(f: Flag[\true\]): ZZ32 = f.v
end
object O extends Unflags end
run(): () = do
    println("MBoolTrait start")
    println("MBoolTrait trait method: " O.unflagTrue(Flag[\true\](8)))
  end
end
EOF
cat > MBoolTop.fss <<'EOF'
component MBoolTop
export Executable
(* a top-level function whose parameter type has a bool static argument, and an object with a field of such a type *)
object Flag[\bool b\](v: ZZ32) end
unflagTrue(f: Flag[\true\]): ZZ32 = f.v
object Holder(f: Flag[\true\])
  get(): ZZ32 = f.v
end
run(): () = do
    println("MBoolTop start")
    println("MBoolTop function: " unflagTrue(Flag[\true\](8)))
    println("MBoolTop field: " Holder(Flag[\true\](9)).get())
  end
end
EOF
cat > MExpectedNew.fss <<'EOF'
component MExpectedNew
export Executable
(* a generic method's static parameter that only the result mentions, with and without a declared type *)
object BoxT[\T\]() end
object Fac
  mk[\T\](): BoxT[\T\] = BoxT[\T\]()
end
mkF[\T\](): BoxT[\T\] = BoxT[\T\]()
run(): () = do
    println("MExpectedNew method, no context: " Fac.mk())
    println("MExpectedNew function, no context: " mkF())
    a: BoxT[\ZZ64\] = Fac.mk()
    println("MExpectedNew method, declared: " a)
  end
end
EOF

end
object Ob[\S\]() extends Tr[\S\] end
run(): () = do
    println("MTraitBoundGen start")
    println("MTraitBoundGen pick: " Ob[\Shape\]().pick(Circle))

end
EOF

A size symbol stays in the mangled name and needs no descriptor. Only a literal size reaches the class loader, which takes its descriptor from `RTTIsize.of` (F-129). Detail: `perf-probes/nat/java.md` sections 1 to 3.
60:- F-67 **The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters.** A size is a symbol, a literal or an operation on sizes, compared by its written form once numerals are folded (F-146). The checker refuses a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` parameter by name. It refuses a size that a call leaves unknown, also in an overload set (F-69). It builds P-40. ## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.

content.content:
### 5.1 Dispatch on declared domains (answer 9; defect 1)

`bestMatchInternal` (`OverloadedFunction.java:1161-1213`) still finds each applicable declaration as before, a generic one instantiated at the arguments by `inferByUnification`. It now keeps a candidate when `moreSpecificDeclaration` (`:1335-1342`) prefers it, where it used to compare the two instances' domains.

- **When one of the two is an own generic**, the comparison is on declared domains. `declaredBelow` (`:1314-1323`) tells whether one declared domain lies inside the other, and when exactly one does, that one wins.
- **Otherwise** the instances' domains are compared, as before. Two plain declarations are always compared that way, since for them the instance is the declaration.
- **A generic declaration's declared domain** is its symbolic instantiation, each type parameter standing for itself with its bounds as its supertypes (`GenericFunctionOrConstructor.getDomain`).
- **A domain lies inside a generic one** when walk's inference, from values that carry only its types, finds an instance whose domain holds them (`instanceHolding`, `:1291-1306`).
- **Results are memoized** per overloaded function for pairs whose domains do not depend on the call (`:1344-1361`).

Why the choice no longer depends on the order: the loop keeps a candidate only when it is strictly preferred to the best so far. When one applicable declaration's declared domain lies below every other's, the loop reaches it in any order and no later candidate displaces it. The load check's rules guarantee such a declaration for a valid set. This is the ordered candidate family the proof addendum applies to (`explorations/reviews/comprises-type-level-proof-addendum.md`, "Application to the existing brief"). Where the declared domains do not order two candidates, the instances decide as before.

component MethodStaticArgDeclaredDomain
export Executable

(* A generic dotted method and a plain one of one name, one inherited and one the object's own, are chosen between on the parameter types they declare: the plain one where its type holds the argument, the generic one elsewhere. *)

trait Shape comprises { Circle, Square } end
object Circle extends Shape end
object Square extends Shape end

trait Describes
    describe[\T extends Shape\](x: T): String = "generic"
end
object Describer extends Describes
    describe(x: Circle): String = "circle"
end

trait Labels
    label(x: Circle): String = "circle"
end
object Labeler extends Labels
    label[\T extends Shape\](x: T): String = "generic"
end

run(): () = do
    assert(Describer.describe(Circle), "circle", "the object's plain method on Circle lies inside the inherited generic method's declared domain, so a Circle takes it; overloading.tex, section \"Applicability to Dotted Method Calls\"")
    assert(Describer.describe(Square), "generic", "only the inherited generic method applies to a Square, with T = Square")
    assert(Labeler.label(Circle), "circle", "the inherited plain method on Circle lies inside the object's generic method's declared domain, so a Circle takes it")
    assert(Labeler.label(Square), "generic", "only the object's generic method applies to a Square")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

content.content:
262:- Resolution: `array1` and `array2` give a `Vector` or a `Matrix` only at `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ`, `RR32` and `RR64`. At every other element type they give a plain array, also at a user type that extends `Number`. Walk stops at a plain array's `+` and unary `-` with a failed dispatch. Under walk, a `T` inferred from a `ZZ32` value is walk's run-time type `Int`, not `ZZ32`. So `array1` and `array2` with an inferred element type give a plain array, where the specification gives a vector (ledger row 721). Write the static argument to get a vector. The factories choose by a `typecase` over a witness, a value of their result type. A `typecase` over a value of the element type matched a type below a number type, and its `cast` threw `CastError`. `aggregate.tex` still states the rule at `Number`.

The rule stated is the one by which the dispatcher of the type group's paper of
2019 instantiates a declaration (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu, ``Polymorphic
Symmetric Multiple Dispatch with Variance'', POPL 2019); the team had assumed
the union of the lower bounds and could not prove it correct.
Both implementations of the revival take the dynamic type of the argument where
the value does not fix the type parameter: the interpreter because it has no
static types, and so no static type of the call to bound the instance, as with
its choice of coercions (\secref{resolving-coercion}); the compiled path because
its dispatcher reads the static arguments of a dispatched declaration from the
value and is not given the static type of the call.
Where the value fixes the type parameter, the two rules give the same instance.
which the compiled type checker applies, with its Return Type Rule checked over
every instance of the less specific declaration; the pair refused above has the
shape of that paper's own example, which the compiled path used to accept and
then fail to verify.
Neither implementation runs the pair allowed above today: the interpreter
refuses it at load, since it asks two declarations with static
parameters for a pair of parameter types that exclude each other (row~159 of the
revival's gap ledger), and the compiled code generator fails on it (row~537).
The compiled implementation adds one restriction that is not a rule of the
language.
